questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to go a place where I could learn and get better at english as well as a different culture from the danish. 
I also looked into how the campus and teaching would differ to the way back home and which experiences besides uni the place offered.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I used the forms online from KU, was a part of their meeting online as well as used to website of the university I was approved for.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed some assistance regarding courses. I wrote GoGlobal an email and also had the opportunity to drop by their office on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: No I would not say so. I applied for the on campus housing, but unfortunately did not get it because of the amount of exchange students this term. We were almost 50% from KU who did not get it. It is the easiest and probably also cheapest way to live in Vancouver. Me and some of the others who did not get housing on campus used facebook - there is a lot of groups with apartments for rental - and be patient. It was a bit tricky to do from home, and be aware of possibly scam! A lot found housing after arrival and stayed at the hostel near UBC while searching (Jericho Beach).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive in Vancouver and you should consider what you would like the most - to live downtown, Kits, West Point. All has its pros and cons. I lived off campus but really close to campus which I liked. Also be prepared that the standards at a reasonably price are not very high - but since it is only 4 months I would say the most important thing is good roommates.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not enough housing for the amount of students - not really a lot of help from UBC regarding finding alternative housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I recieved a file from UBC and had to prioritize my top 10 courses - they wanted 10 to be sure you got accepted into some. They registered me in 4 courses and I did not have to do more in the beginning.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail and in person help if needed - before and after arriving.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into my top 4 classes, and had to drop one during the first 2 weeks.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration is pretty slow, and different faculties register at different times. Do not worry if you do not get into a course you want in the beginning, you also got the chance during the first weeks to add and drop courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of my courses were fine. They were all level 300 and gave me a lot of new knowledge.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. A lot of my courses were lectures (with 100-200 students) and then online quizzes, cases, assignments and discussion posts. The grade you get can be based on participation and the other things you have to do during the semester and not just a final exam. You have the possibility of a lot of hours with TA's and the profs to ask questions if needed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FNH 313 - Food Microbiology
MICB 302 - Immunology
MICB 306 - Molecular Virology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the Molecular Virology with Dr. Jean and prof. Graves. Really interesting to learn more about viruses. Great combination of general knowledge and applying that to specific well known viruses in the second half of the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Mostly having to buy myself stuff to be able to go e.g. camping, skiing, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food were way more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: the AMS UBC have more than +250 different clubs - sports, cultural groups, creative groups and way more - almost all you can think of. They are also good at promoting them in the beginning of the term. It can be a bit complicated and overwhelming to find out what to join because of the many opportunitues - but most clubs are open for late joining too. AMS also planned a lot of other fun things to join - quizzes, painting, yoga etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would look out for the exchange club! Good opportunities to do fun stuff with your fellow exchange students.
I joined the badminton and also tried the knitting and sewing club.
I was a part of the VOC - varsity outdoor club - were you can join different trips and rent gear.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature around Vancouver! In the summer you can hike and in the winter you can ski. I absolutely loved the nature and it is easy to plan and go places - look into setting up accounts for Turo or Evo to be able to get a car.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did not find it hard to adjust. Vancouver is very multi cultural and everybody is very nice and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everyone are very friendly, do not be scared to talk to people in your classes or join clubs and get to know people that way.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: NA

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness among almost everyone.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You can find a lot of used stuff in different thrift stores around kits and downtown - but I was surprised how much I was using my sleeping bag and hiking boots, so if you got them at home bring them with you!

The weather changes a lot, we had the hottest summer and then a lot of snow. It rains a lot too, apparently more than in Denmark. 

Be prepared for a busy schedule, there is a lot of things going on all the time and a lot of trips to go on!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Prepare yourself for the biggest adventure. UBC is big and there is a lot of opportunities and things you can do almost everyday. I used instagram a lot and found the different accounts and they proved helpful with a lot of information. Be openminded and join trips with fellow students - we used whatsapp to arrange stuff.

It is really nice to have a car for trips, a lot of other fellow students bought cars and sold them before going home,.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To stay up to date with studies. I studied a lot alone because everyone seems to have different schedules. I missed a study group.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: This was the best and most amazing experience! GO GO GO.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
